Let me analyze the conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Avery Berkel"
- Document: "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd"

Now, the certificate text embedded in the context includes comments: `<!-- applicant: Avery Berkel -->` — wait, the embedded metadata comment says applicant: Avery Berkel. But the "document" field for the conflict says the document says "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd". Presumably the certificate body text (beyond the excerpt shown) says "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd".

Is "Avery Berkel" the same entity as "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd"? Avery Berkel is a brand/company; Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd is the legal entity name. Historically, Avery Berkel was a company formed from merger; Weigh-Tronix acquired Avery Berkel, and the company was known as Avery Weigh-Tronix. Avery Berkel is a brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix. These are related but are they the same entity? The rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity."

"Avery Berkel" vs "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" — these are different names. Avery Berkel is a brand; Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd is the parent company. However, in practice, OIML certificates issued by GB1 (NWML) for Avery scales: applicant could be listed as "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" while the register simplified to "Avery Berkel". Are these "genuinely different company or person names"? Avery Berkel Limited was a legal company name; Avery Weigh-Tronix is also a legal name (formerly Avery Berkel). They trace to the same business lineage but are technically distinct legal entities at different times.

Hmm. The fused record: which value should it carry? The rule says genuinely different names = different-entity with best_value = document's. But is this genuinely different? Avery Berkel and Avery Weigh-Tronix are arguably the same company rebranded: Avery Berkel became Avery Weigh-Tronix after Weigh-Tronix acquired weighing division. Actually history: GDA (GEC) sold Avery Berkel to Weigh-Tronix in 2000; it became Avery Weigh-Tronix. The brand "Avery Berkel" continues as a brand under Avery Weigh-Tronix. In 2009, the certificate applicant would be "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" legally, and "Avery Berkel" is the brand. So the register's "Avery Berkel" is a brand shorthand for the same applicant.

Given the certificate is the legal instrument, and document says "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd", the best value should be the document's value if we deem them the same entity (the register using a brand name). The rules give same-entity for spelling drift etc. This is more than spelling drift — it's a brand vs legal entity name. But the certificate itself in the metadata comment says applicant: Avery Berkel. Hmm, the embedded comment is extraction artifact, likely mirroring register.

The decision: I'd say "same-entity" — Avery Berkel is the trading brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd, same company; best_value = document's "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" because certificate is legal instrument. The verdict options: same-entity allows best_value to be either register canonical (for number/year formats) or document (for names?). The rules specify best_value for same-entity only explicitly for number/year (register canonical) and document-noise (register). For same-entity name drift, presumably either; but given the certificate is the legal instrument and it says "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd", the fused record should carry the document's legal name.

Alternatively "different-entity" would also pick document's value. The verdict matters for semantics: is it genuinely a different company? I think not genuinely different — same business, brand vs legal name. I'll go with same-entity, best_value "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd", why: Avery Berkel is the trading brand of the same company whose legal name on the certificate is Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd, so keep the certificate's legal name.

One sentence, short.
